name: DataRoom Live
description: Collaborative CSV quality review with workspace permissions, explainable detectors, assignments, comments, and activity history.
summary: Teams inspect dataset profiles and treat automated findings as review signals. Workspace permissions, assignments, comments, and issue activity support shared decisions about data quality.
architecture: Next.js handles authenticated workspace workflows with Supabase SSR sessions. CSV files remain in private Supabase Storage; csv-parse produces server-side profiles and deterministic quality findings. Supabase PostgreSQL and row-level security protect workspace metadata and review records. No LLM powers detection.

capabilities.name: CSV profiling
capabilities.description: Validate uploads and inspect types, missingness, uniqueness, and column statistics.

capabilities.name: Collaborative review
capabilities.description: Assign issues, comment, change resolution status, and inspect activity history.

capabilities.name: Workspace access
capabilities.description: Apply authenticated owner, admin, member, and viewer permissions.

stack.usage: App Router pages and server operations coordinate dataset review and sensitive mutations.
Reusable components display issues, assignments, comments, and dataset details.
TypeScript describes CSV profiles, detector findings, and workspace records.
Supabase Auth manages sessions; private Storage holds CSVs and RLS restricts workspace tables.
Supabase PostgreSQL stores column profiles, issues, comments, and workspace activity.
csv-parse reads validated uploads for profiling and deterministic detectors.

architectureConnections.description: Server-side sessions authorize workspace operations and uploads.
Computed profiles and issue metadata are persisted; raw CSVs stay in Storage.
